question: Predict the secondary structure of an RNA sequence using RNAfold (with the -p flag to generate a dot-plot file), then visualize the square root of base-pairing probabilities as a square heatmap.

files.eval_guideline: Square heatmap with nucleotide positions on both axes and cells colored by sqrt(base-pairing probability); color scheme and styling may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The candidate has the exact same basename and .ps.png image format as the reference. Its name specifically identifies the RNAfold dot-plot visualization for human tRNA-Phe, matching the task context.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires semantic plot content—a square heatmap with nucleotide positions on both axes and cell colors representing square-root base-pairing probabilities—while explicitly allowing visual styling and color-scheme differences. Pixel-level or record-level matching would therefore be inappropriate.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images present a square 83-nucleotide RNA base-pairing matrix and encode the square root of RNAfold -p base-pair probabilities by cell color. The characteristic paired-stem diagonals and weaker alternative-pairing patterns correspond across the two plots. The main differences are representational: the reference uses approximately 0-based positions with the y-axis increasing upward, whereas the candidate uses 1-based nucleotide positions and an image-style y-axis increasing downward. Thus the same symmetric pair relationships appear vertically reflected in the rendered heatmap. The colormaps and normalization also differ: the reference uses dark-to-yellow viridis with a displayed upper range below 1, while the candidate uses white-to-blue with a fixed 0–1 scale. The candidate explicitly labels the colorbar as sqrt(base-pairing probability), while the reference labels it more generically as base-pairing probability. Titles, fonts, and spacing differ, but both axes are appropriately labeled and the scientific content and interpretation are preserved. No critical data or required element is missing.
